solution:
The correct answer is __**1 - a, 2 - b, 3 - c, 4 - d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kashi:** Its capital was **Varanasi**, a prominent cultural and religious city in ancient India, known for its association with Hinduism and Buddhism.
 
• **Kosala:** The capital of Kosala was **Shravasti**, a major city during the time of Buddha and a significant center for Buddhist teachings.
 
• **Avanti:** Its capital was **Ujjayini (Ujjain)**, which was a major trade and cultural hub in ancient India, later becoming an important center for Hinduism.
 
• **Magadha:** The capital of Magadha was **Rajagriha (modern-day Rajgir)**, known for its role in the emergence of Jainism and Buddhism.
 
• These Janapadas were among the sixteen Mahajanapadas, ancient kingdoms mentioned in Buddhist and Jain texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kashi:**
 
 
• Kashi (Varanasi) was one of the most renowned cities of ancient India and was famous for its learning, spirituality, and trade.
 
• It is considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
 
• The city also played a pivotal role in the spread of Buddhism and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Kosala:**
 
 
• Kosala was an important kingdom, often mentioned in ancient Indian texts like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• Shravasti, its capital, was a prominent center of Buddhist teachings and practices, with Buddha spending many monsoon seasons there.
 
• The Kosala region was also known for its prosperity and rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Avanti:**
 
 
• Avanti was one of the most significant Mahajanapadas of ancient India, divided into two parts, with Ujjayini being the northern capital.
 
• Ujjayini was a hub for trade routes and an important city for astronomy and mathematics, housing famous scholars like Varahamihira.
 
• The region played a crucial role in the spread of Jainism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Magadha:**
 
 
• Magadha emerged as one of the most powerful kingdoms of ancient India, forming the core of several great empires, including the Maurya and Gupta empires.
 
• Rajagriha (Rajgir), its capital, was known for its fortifications and association with Jainism and Buddhism.
 
• Later, Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) replaced Rajagriha as the capital under the Maurya Empire.
